title: Adwind_jRAT_Incident_Response_Scenario_27a
description: Investigate and respond to a potential security incident involving the Adwind/jRAT trojan on a victim host.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The victim host in your network has exhibited unusual behavior, including unexpected network connections and suspicious process activity. Your task is to investigate and respond to this potential security incident involving the Adwind/jRAT trojan. You will need to find text-type flags named 'service_name', 'timer_name', and 'filename'.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the victim host with the following credentials:
- Hostname: victim
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

Enter the word 'start' to proceed to the next level.
levels.local_content:
You have SSH access to the victim host with the following credentials:
- Hostname: victim
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

Enter the word 'start' to proceed to the next level.

levels.title: Investigate Suspicious Services
levels.content: Investigate the victim host for unauthorized or suspicious services that may indicate trojan activity.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Systemd services can be listed using systemctl commands.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use systemctl to list all services and look for anything unusual.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: The command to list services is: systemctl list-units --type=service

levels.title: Identify Scheduled Tasks or Timers
levels.content: Determine if any scheduled tasks or timers are responsible for automatically executing the malware on the victim host.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Systemd timers can be listed using systemctl commands.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use systemctl to list all timers and look for anything unusual.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: The command to list timers is: systemctl list-timers

levels.title: Locate Malware Files
levels.content: Locate files installed by the malware on the victim host that may provide further evidence of the compromise.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Malware often creates or modifies shell scripts.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Search for shell scripts in the filesystem.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: The command to find shell scripts is: find / -name '*.sh' 2>/dev/null
